title: Computational-Statistical Gaps in Reinforcement Learning
review_status: full-text audit complete; reduction assumptions, complexity results, oracle model, statistical counterpoint, and remaining open bound checked
sections_checked: Sections 1.1.1-1.1.2 main lower bounds and open problem
Section 1.1 definitions of Linear-k-RL, horizon, action count, oracle access and objective
Sections 2-3 Unique-3-SAT reductions and simulator details
venue_year_verified: arXiv v2 dated 2022-07-03; venue not independently checked
evidence_note: Unless NP=RP, no randomized polynomial-time algorithm for the defined deterministic-transition Linear-2-RL setting (two/three actions, H=O(d), linear V*/Q*, given reward/transition/feature access); rETH yields a quasi-polynomial lower bound. Paper distinguishes computational hardness from polynomial-query statistical feasibility and leaves exponential rETH lower bound open. Does not establish identical hardness for stochastic transitions or practical systems.

title: Approximating Edit Distance in the Fully Dynamic Model
review_status: full-text audit complete; update model, parameterized approximation/update bound, probability guarantee, and asymptotic regimes checked
sections_checked: Introduction and model of arbitrary insert/delete/substitute updates
Conclusion and cited fully dynamic string-algorithm context
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2023-07-14; venue not independently checked
evidence_note: For strings of length at most n, integer 2≤b≤n gives O(b log_b n)-approximation, amortized expected update time b²(log n)^{O(log_b n)}, and correctness with probability at least 1−1/n. This is an asymptotic theorem, not a real-workload runtime/quality evaluation.
